title: Push, Pull & Motion
description: Grade 3 Science: forces, push and pull, motion, friction, gravity and magnets. How forces make things move, stop and change — with sorting games and experiments.

topics.title: Forces: Pushes and Pulls
topics.concept:
A force is simply a push or a pull. We use forces all day long, often without noticing:

  • 👐 A push moves something away from you (pushing a door, kicking a ball).
  • 🤝 A pull brings something towards you (pulling a rope, opening a drawer).

Nothing moves, stops or changes direction by itself — a force has to act on it.

recap: A force is a push or a pull.
A push moves things away; a pull brings things closer.
Things move or stop only when a force acts on them.

wonder.text: To open a drawer you pull it; to close it you push it. Every day you use a hidden helper called a force.

qa.q: Is kicking a ball a push or a pull?
qa.a: A kick is a push! Your foot pushes the ball away from you, so it rolls forward. A push always moves something away.

qa.q: Can a force be big or small?
qa.a: Yes! A gentle push moves a light toy a little. A big, strong push is needed to move something heavy like a full box. Bigger force, bigger effect.

topics.title: Forces Change Motion
topics.concept:
Forces can change the motion (movement) of things in several ways:

  • ▶️ Start a still thing moving (kicking a ball).
  • ⏹️ Stop a moving thing (catching a ball).
  • 🔄 Change its direction (hitting a ball with a bat).
  • ⚡ Make it go faster or slower.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 330 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="330" height="150" fill="#f7faff"/><text x="55" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">▶️</text><text x="55" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Start</text><text x="165" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">⏹️</text><text x="165" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Stop</text><text x="275" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🔄</text><text x="275" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Turn</text><text x="165" y="138" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#555" text-anchor="middle">Forces change how things move</text></svg>
recap: Forces can start, stop, speed up, slow or turn a moving thing.
A kick starts motion; catching stops it.
Forces can also change an object's shape.

wonder.text: A football lying still suddenly flies across the field. What made it start moving?

qa.q: How does a goalkeeper stop a ball?
qa.a: The goalkeeper's hands push against the moving ball with a force. That force stops the ball's motion — no more goal!

qa.q: Can a force change shape too?
qa.a: Yes! Squashing clay or stretching a rubber band uses a force that changes their shape, not just their motion. Forces are powerful helpers.

topics.title: Friction Slows Things Down
topics.concept:
Friction is a force that slows down moving things when two surfaces rub together.

  • 🛑 More friction on rough surfaces (a ball stops quickly on grass or a road).
  • ⛸️ Less friction on smooth surfaces (a ball slides far on ice or a marble floor).

Friction can be helpful too — it lets us walk without slipping and helps brakes stop a bicycle!
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="320" height="150" fill="#f7fff7"/><rect y="100" width="160" height="50" fill="#bfe3a0"/><rect x="160" y="100" width="160" height="50" fill="#d8f0ff"/><text x="70" y="86" font-size="28" text-anchor="middle">⚽</text><text x="250" y="86" font-size="28" text-anchor="middle">⚽</text><text x="80" y="134" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#3f7a2f" text-anchor="middle">Rough: stops fast</text><text x="240" y="134" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#1f7fe0" text-anchor="middle">Smooth: slides far</text></svg>
recap: Friction is a force that slows moving things down.
Rough surfaces have more friction; smooth surfaces have less.
Friction also helps us walk and stop without slipping.

wonder.text: Roll a ball on a rough road and on smooth ice. Why does one stop so much sooner?

qa.a: Both! Friction slows things down, which can be a nuisance. But it also helps us — we can grip, walk and stop a bike because of friction. Without it, we would slip everywhere!
Ice is very smooth, so there is very little friction. With almost nothing to slow them down, our feet slide easily — that is why we slip on ice.

topics.title: Gravity Pulls Things Down
topics.concept:
Gravity is a pulling force from the Earth that pulls everything down towards the ground.

  • 🍎 A dropped apple falls down, never up.
  • ⬇️ Gravity is why things have weight and why we stay on the ground.
  • 🌍 The bigger the object (like Earth), the stronger its pull.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 280 160" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="280" height="160" fill="#eef6ff"/><rect y="130" width="280" height="30" fill="#cfe3c0"/><text x="140" y="50" font-size="30" text-anchor="middle">🍎</text><defs><marker id="gr3" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="4" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0 L9 4 L0 8 z" fill="#e53935"/></marker></defs><g stroke="#e53935" stroke-width="4" marker-end="url(#gr3)"><line x1="140" y1="68" x2="140" y2="116"/></g><text x="178" y="96" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#c0392b">Gravity</text></svg>
recap: Gravity is Earth's pull towards the ground.
It makes dropped things fall down, not up.
Gravity gives objects their weight and keeps us on Earth.

wonder.text: Throw a ball up as high as you can. Why does it always come back down?

qa.q: Why don't we float off the Earth?
qa.a: Earth's gravity constantly pulls us down towards its centre, holding us firmly on the ground. That is why we can walk, run and jump back down safely.
Far out in space, away from Earth, gravity is very weak, so astronauts float! That is why everything drifts around inside a spaceship.

topics.title: Magnets Push and Pull
topics.concept:
A magnet is special — it can pull (attract) some things without even touching them.

  • 🧲 Magnets attract things made of iron and steel (pins, nails, paper clips).
  • 🚫 Magnets do NOT attract wood, plastic, paper or rubber.
  • ↔️ Two magnets can attract (pull together) or repel (push apart), depending on which ends face each other.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="320" height="150" fill="#f7f7ff"/><path d="M40 40 v40 a20 20 0 0 0 40 0 v-40 h-12 v40 a8 8 0 0 1 -16 0 v-40 z" fill="#e53935"/><text x="96" y="66" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle">📎</text><text x="110" y="66" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle">📎</text><text x="70" y="120" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#c0392b" text-anchor="middle">Attracts iron</text><rect x="200" y="55" width="34" height="22" fill="#e53935"/><rect x="250" y="55" width="34" height="22" fill="#3CA7FF"/><g stroke="#888" stroke-width="2"><line x1="236" y1="66" x2="248" y2="66"/></g><text x="242" y="120" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#555" text-anchor="middle">Push apart</text></svg>
recap: Magnets attract things made of iron and steel.
Magnets do not attract wood, plastic or paper.
Two magnets can attract (pull) or repel (push apart).

wonder.text: Hold two magnets together one way and they stick; turn one around and they push apart. How?

qa.q: Will a magnet pick up a plastic spoon?
qa.a: No. Magnets only attract things made of iron or steel. A plastic spoon, a wooden pencil or a paper sheet will not stick to a magnet.

qa.q: Why do two magnets sometimes push apart?
qa.a: Every magnet has two ends (poles). Same poles push apart (repel), and opposite poles pull together (attract). Flip one magnet and you feel the push or the pull!

questions.explanation: A force is simply a push or a pull.

questions.q: Kicking a ball away from you is a…
questions.explanation: A kick pushes the ball away — it is a push.

questions.q: The force that slows moving things down is…
questions.explanation: Friction slows moving things when surfaces rub together.
Gravity is Earth's pull, pulling everything down.
Magnets attract iron and steel things, like a steel key.
Smooth ice has little friction, so the ball rolls far.

questions.q: Why can we walk without slipping?
options: Because friction between our feet and the ground grips
questions.explanation: Friction between our feet and the ground gives grip so we do not slip.

questions.q: Two magnets pushed apart are showing…
questions.explanation: Same poles of magnets repel — they push apart.

questions.q: Why do astronauts float in space?
options: Gravity is very weak far from Earth
questions.explanation: Far from Earth, gravity is very weak, so astronauts float.

questions.q: Hitting a moving ball with a bat changes its…
questions.explanation: The bat's force changes the ball's direction of motion.

questions.q: Which set lists things a magnet will NOT attract?
questions.explanation: Magnets do not attract wood, plastic or paper.
